title: Inventory environment variables and placeholder requirements
description: Create a verified inventory of application and installer environment variable names and ensure project-local templates contain placeholders only.
acceptanceCriteria: Every `process.env` name used by application/runtime TypeScript is listed with its source file and purpose
Every installer/update/bootstrap variable is listed with its default and whether it is secret
`apps/web/.env.local.example` contains only safe placeholders and no real values
Documentation distinguishes runtime, installer, and test-only variables

steps.details: Search `apps/web` and `packages` for `process.env` and record each name, source file, default, and whether it is sensitive.
Search `scripts/*.sh` for parameter defaults and assignments; record version, architecture, mirror, path, and secret variables without values from an installed host.
Add only missing safe placeholder entries to `apps/web/.env.local.example`; do not copy values from `apps/web/.env.local`.
Add a concise environment inventory to the release documentation or evidence, explicitly stating that real values must be entered manually on the VPS/local host.

technicalNotes: Evidence: `.agent/evidence/environment-inventory.md` records all observed application/runtime names and installer inputs.
Template: `apps/web/.env.local.example` contains only safe example paths/placeholders; real `.env.local` values were not read or recorded.
Verification: independent scanner found no required runtime name missing from the template or inventory, and confirmed secret placeholders.
Do not add a real value, token, password, key, or production connection string to this task or evidence.
